clue.text: Drug injection for pop

blocks.note: pot is slang for cannabis
a shot is a jab with a needle

explanation.surface: Someone takes a drug injection to get a quick high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' is a noun here: to have a pop at something is to take a quick shot at it.
explanation.definitionFit: A potshot is a casual, random attempt or shot, which is informally a pop.

clue.text: After last of lasagna, tagliatelle perhaps

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: past as in 'half past', meaning after
the closing letter of lasagna

explanation.surface: After finishing the lasagne, someone moves on to tagliatelle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagliatelle is one kind of pasta, a flat ribbon noodle; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Seawards in crude raft, marines could show you a hatchery

indicators.note: something crude is rough and unrefined, so the letters are knocked out of shape
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written for its letters
a boat heading seawards is going out
RM is the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Marines paddling a makeshift raft out to sea come across a fish nursery.
explanation.definitionFit: A trout farm breeds and rears fish, so it is a type of hatchery.

clue.text: Strongly disliked bowler, English, opener for Derbyshire?

indicators.note: an opener comes first, so the initial letter is used

blocks.note: a bowler is a rounded felt hat
E is the abbreviation for English
the first letter of Derbyshire

explanation.surface: An English bowler opening for Derbyshire, an English county cricket team, was loathed.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture (bowler, opener) is a trap: the bowler is a hat, which Americans call a derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Hated is the past tense of hate, to detest or loathe intensely.

clue.text: Article on genius from Australia making a film

blocks.note: the definite article
a wizard is a brilliant expert
of means from, and Oz is slang for Australia

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about an Australian genius who makes a film.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the article above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wizard of Oz is the 1939 musical movie starring Judy Garland.

clue.text: Proust slipped into a state of unconsciousness

indicators.note: letters that have slipped have fallen out of their proper places

blocks.note: the French novelist's name, used for its letters

explanation.surface: The novelist Proust lapses into a faint.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed condition of near or total insensibility.

clue.text: Four-letter word used by girl upset about first of tasks

indicators.note: in a down clue an upset thing is turned upside down, so read from the bottom up
about means around, so one word goes round another
first of picks out only the opening letter of the following word

blocks.note: a girl's name
the first letter of tasks

explanation.surface: A girl annoyed by her first assignment resorts to swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an expletive, but a tetragram is simply any word of four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetragram comes from Greek for four letters, naming a word made of that many letters.

clue.text: Whelp I left for student

blocks.note: a whelp is a young dog
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A puppy was abandoned in place of a student.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil is a learner, especially a schoolchild.

clue.text: Girl in race, one across imaginary kingdom

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a run is a race
a girl's name
the Roman numeral for one
A is the crossword abbreviation for across

explanation.surface: A girl running a race, one of several crossing a fantasy land.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruritania is the fictional central European kingdom of Anthony Hope's The Prisoner of Zenda.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruritania is invented, so it is a fictional realm, and its name now stands for any such made-up country.

clue.text: Not lasting long, something enjoyed by pupils?

blocks.note: first meaning: temporary, brief in duration
second meaning, read as two words: a brief school session, which pupils would welcome

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: a school term that is short.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated adjective means temporary; split into two words it is a brief period of school.

clue.text: Game at which children always leave one standing?

definitions.text: Game at which children always leave one standing?

blocks.clueFragment: Game at which children always leave one standing?
blocks.note: surface reading: children who are so good at a game that they always outclass someone
setter's reading: literally, every round one player is left on their feet with no seat when the music stops

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave one standing' usually means beat easily; here it means someone literally has nowhere to sit.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a party game where players circle seats and scramble for one fewer seat than people each round.

clue.text: Spill drop of rum by video

indicators.note: a drop is the smallest amount, so only one letter of the drink is taken, its first

blocks.note: video tape, as in old recordings
the opening letter of rum

explanation.surface: Someone knocks over a little rum next to the video player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spill' looks like a verb but is a noun: a spill is a thin strip of wood or paper for lighting a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A taper is a slender wick or strip used to carry a flame, the same object as a spill.

clue.text: Book in Saturday's client in need of treatment

indicators.note: something in need of treatment must be worked on and reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A weekend patient's notes in a book, the client needing medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: A Study in Scarlet is Arthur Conan Doyle's first Sherlock Holmes novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the title of a novel, so it is an example of a book.

clue.text: Gather a large amount

blocks.note: taken as written
a mass is a large quantity

explanation.surface: An instruction to collect a great deal of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase, but the definition is the first word and the rest spells the answer piece by piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect or accumulate, a synonym of gather.

clue.text: A goddess paid her to, in error

indicators.note: in error means wrongly done, so the letters are set out wrongly

blocks.note: taken as written for its letters

explanation.surface: A deity was paid by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite is the Greek goddess of love and beauty.

clue.text: Chap Tyson dealt with, a toady

indicators.note: dealt with suggests cards dealt out, so the letters are distributed afresh

blocks.note: taken as written for its letters

explanation.surface: The boxer Mike Tyson sorted out a creep.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant is a flatterer who fawns on the powerful, just as a toady does.

clue.text: Find out when? Sure

blocks.note: as in 'as I arrived' means when I arrived
sure and certain are synonyms

explanation.surface: A quick exchange: asking when to discover something, and an agreeable reply.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to establish or discover a fact for certain.

clue.text: Sounds like a combination of notes by one playing instrument

indicators.note: sounds like tells us to go by how the words are spoken

blocks.note: a chord is notes played together, said quickly like a word for agreement
the Roman numeral for one
a record or show that is playing is on

explanation.surface: A description of chords played by a musician on an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The accordion is a squeezebox, a bellows-driven musical instrument with keys or buttons.

clue.text: Murderous child - I am treated without love

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A neglected child, unloved, turns violent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but the O for love must be added to the letters of child and I am before they are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Homicidal means inclined to kill, which is what murderous describes.

clue.text: Coffee (instant) and tea

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, an instant
cha is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A menu offering instant coffee and tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instant' looks like a type of coffee, but it means a moment: in British speech 'half a mo' is half a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a type of coffee, originally from the Yemeni port of that name.

clue.text: In a state of great elation at the North Pole?

definitions.text: In a state of great elation

blocks.clueFragment: In a state of great elation
blocks.note: first meaning: an idiom for feeling extremely happy
second meaning, taken literally: positioned at the very top of the globe

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the literal reading of the idiom, since maps put the North Pole at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means euphoric, and literally describes standing at the topmost point of Earth.

clue.text: Circuitous tour round duke's house

indicators.note: circuitous means winding about, so the letters wander from their order
round means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: taken as written for its letters, then rearranged
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A winding tour around a duke's stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is a royal dynasty, not a building; the Tudors ruled England from 1485 to 1603.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were an English royal family, and royal families are called houses.

clue.text: Bet salary on foremost of runners

indicators.note: the foremost is the one at the front, so the initial letter is taken

blocks.note: a wage is pay
the first letter of runners

explanation.surface: Someone gambles their pay on the leading horse.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the salary above the runners' letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A wager is a stake placed on an outcome, which is a bet.

clue.text: Drop it in front of Dominican church

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: the first letter of Dominican
taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave something at the door of a Dominican church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In front of' looks like one phrase meaning before, but it splits: 'it' goes in, and 'front of' takes a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch something is to abandon or discard it, to drop it.

clue.text: Home help returned from Asian country

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
aid is help

explanation.surface: A domestic helper has come back from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home help' reads as one job title, but it splits in two, and only the help is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a nation in South Asia.

clue.text: Relish acquiring one gite abroad in today's climate?

indicators.note: abroad suggests being all over the place, so the letters are scattered
acquiring means taking in, so one word holds the others inside it

blocks.note: zest is enthusiasm or relish
the Roman numeral for one
a gite is a French holiday cottage, used for its letters

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys buying a holiday cottage overseas in the current economic climate.
explanation.walkthrough: The German loanword means the spirit of the age; the question mark admits the definition is a loose paraphrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The zeitgeist is the prevailing mood or outlook of a particular era, here the present one.

clue.text: Rotten type, in time, may cause mistakes in print

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is a nasty, untrustworthy person

explanation.surface: A careless typesetter, given time, will produce printing errors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' points to printing, but here a rotten type is a disreputable person.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are listed corrections for errors found in a printed book.

clue.text: Decisive moment following onset of storm - squeeze together

indicators.note: the onset of something is its beginning, so the first letter is kept
following places one part after another

blocks.note: the first letter of storm
the crunch, as in 'when it comes to the crunch'

explanation.surface: A tense moment as a storm begins and people huddle together.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrunch is to crumple or compress something tightly, such as paper.
